speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me determine the cause, please describe exactly how the spinning sensation feels and what triggers it. Also, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To further evaluate the cause of your position-dependent vertigo, how long does each episode last, and do you experience any nausea or vomiting during these spells? Please also describe any new neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
